title: Adaptive prefill <-> autoregressive scheduling and KV coordination (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures an experimental design for an adaptive sequencer and KV coordinator that enables safe and efficient overlap between prefill work and autoregressive (decode) work in the serving runtime. Goal is to increase GPU utilization and reduce tail latency for mixed workloads (long prefill batches + low-latency streaming decodes) without regressing cost or correctness.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Workloads at scale are heterogeneous: many requests are short-chat style decodes, others are long-context few-shot prompts that require an expensive prefill. Prefill execution (full context forward pass) is expensive but well-suited to batching. Decodes are latency-sensitive and benefit from lower per-step overhead and smaller micro-batches.
- Today’s simple separation (do prefill offline, then attach KV store and do decode) leaves GPUs idle waiting for prefill aggregation or forces us to serialize decodes behind large prefill batches, increasing tail latency.
- We need a mechanism that: (a) allows prefill micro-batches to start and progress without blocking latency-sensitive decodes, (b) makes intelligent kernel and memory placement decisions for KV shards, (c) maintains KV/attention state consistency, and (d) respects per-stream priority and SLOs.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not attempt to redesign model sharding across nodes (we assume existing tensor/model-parallel placement stays constant).
- Not covering model compilation/inference kernel changes in detail; we only call out kernel-selection constraints that the scheduler should respect.

High-level proposal:
Introduce an adaptive sequencer component (Sequencer) in the request path and a light-weight KV Coordinator (KV-Coordinator) that together implement:
1) Priority-aware admission control and microbatching.
2) Overlapped execution: interleave prefill micro-batches with decode steps on the same GPU, using time-slicing and kernel-aware ordering.
3) Incremental KV writes and read fences so that partly-prefilled KV state is usable by decode requests when safe.
4) Kernel hinting to runtime backend so kernel selection and workspace allocation avoid thrashing.

Core concepts and definitions:
- Prefill micro-batch: a group of prefill requests batched together for a forward pass that builds KV caches.
- Decode step: an autoregressive generation step that consumes KV cache and produces tokens.
- Stream priority: per-request priority class (P0 low-latency interactive, P1 bulk batch, P2 background/housekeeping).
- KV shard: runtime’s in-GPU KV state partition for a given model partition.
- Read fence: a lightweight synchronization point indicating that KV shard is consistent up to a certain sequence index.

Sequencer responsibilities:
- Accepts requests and assigns them to priority lanes.
- Tracks readiness of streams: whether prefill is complete, partially complete, or waiting for aggregation.
- Forms micro-batches for prefill and decode with target sizes that are adaptive based on measured latency/SLO and queue depths.
- Decides when to interleave decode steps between prefill micro-batches based on heuristics (see heuristics below).
- Emits schedule directives to the executor with kernel hints (e.g., prefer-async, workspace-size, inferred fast-kernel preference for int8/qat ops).

KV-Coordinator responsibilities:
- Maintains per-stream KV write markers and exposes read-fence API: can_read(stream_id, index) -> bool.
- Allows partial visibility: a decode may read KV entries up to the last fully-committed layer for that stream; if a prefill has completed layers 0..L-1, decodes may proceed for those layers and pad missing layers with a compact-state representation (fallback).
- Coordinates KV memory reclamation and eviction decisions with the sequencer (hotness signals).

Execution model / timeline example:
1) Several long prefill requests arrive (P1). Sequencer opens a prefill micro-batch and schedules it to GPU.
2) A P0 interactive decode arrives. Sequencer attempts to place it in a small micro-batch for immediate execution.
3) If the GPU is running a prefill micro-batch, Sequencer evaluates preemption policy: can a short decode step be interleaved between prefill kernels without invalidating the prefill’s KV building? If yes, emit an interleave directive (pause prefill kernel at a model boundary or safe kernel split).
4) KV-Coordinator exposes that the prefill has committed layer L; decode can read layers <= L and continue; for missing layers the executor uses one of: a) compute missing layers on-the-fly (if cheap), b) use KV filler path (small warm-start state), or c) stall until commit depending on priority/SLO.

Safety and consistency rules:
- Prefill micro-batches must record per-layer commit points. No reads beyond commit point allowed.
- When a prefill is preempted mid-micro-batch, partial progress is checkpointed in a lightweight commit log so that subsequent decode reads can proceed on stable state.
- If a prefill is aborted, any partial KV writes are rolled back or marked tombstoned so decodes don’t consume inconsistent state.

Heuristics for interleaving decisions (initial set):
- If decode latency SLO < X ms and current prefill micro-batch remaining time > Y ms, try to interleave. X and Y are tunable (runtime defaults: X=80ms, Y=30ms).
- If micro-batch kernel sequence has a known split point (e.g., attention kernel boundaries), allow preemption only at those splits to avoid workspace corruption.
- If estimated single-step kernel (for decode) uses a conflicting workspace size leading to thrashing, prefer scheduling a smaller decode micro-batch or rescheduling prefill instead.
- Allow limited preemptions per prefill micro-batch (configurable budget) to bound fragmentation of prefill GPU efficiency.

KV memory policy notes:
- Prefill-heavy workloads produce many transient KV shards. KV-Coordinator maintains a hot-set LRU per model partition and exposes hint: pin_for_n_steps(stream_id, n).
- When interleaving decodes, we may need to pin the prefix layers’ KV memory while allowing deeper layers to be evicted earlier. Thus per-layer refcounts are necessary.

Kernel hinting and runtime constraints:
- Sequencer should send kernel-hints: expected sequence length distribution, priority, and whether int8/QAT kernels are allowed. The backend can then choose kernel variants that minimize workspace churn when interleaving is likely.
- Executors must expose safe preemption points (kernel split hooks) that the sequencer can call out to pause/resume execution. This is a small API surface: request_preemption_point(gpu_ctx, epoch) -> list of safe_offsets.

Admission control and backpressure:
- Don’t admit more decoding micro-batches than can be reasonably run without causing prefill starvation. Admission uses priority-weighted tokens; P0 streams have tokens that replenish faster.
- If the system detects persistent prefill slowdown caused by frequent preemptions, dynamically increase prefill micro-batch size or lower decode preemption budget for affected model to regain throughput.

Metrics to track (observability):
- P0 tail latency (p95/p99) before and after overlapping enabled.
- Prefill throughput (tokens/sec), micro-batch efficiency (ideal_batch_time / actual_time).
- Preemption rate per prefill micro-batch, percent of prefill work resumed vs restarted.
- KV read-latency and percent of decode steps served from partially-committed KV vs full-prefill.
- Kernel workspace thrash events (times the runtime had to reallocate large workspace due to conflicting kernel sizes).

Experiments and rollout plan:
1) Canary: enable interleaving on a single GPU cluster for a subset of models with synthetic mixed workload. Monitor metrics above.
2) Beta: enable adaptive sequencer with conservative heuristics for internal prod traffic (non-critical).
3) Production ramp: expand policies, expose knobs in Evaluate/Optimize console (batch-size bias, preemption-budget) and run continuous A/B against baseline.

Implementation notes / integration points:
- Sequencer is primarily a control-plane component but must be tightly co-located with the executor to minimize RPC latencies for preemption decisions. Consider co-locating sequencer as a sidecar to the GPU worker process.
- KV-Coordinator maintains an in-memory commit map; persist only metadata for recovery. On worker restart, prefill checkpoints are revalidated by re-running minimal forward passes for the last few layers (fast warmup path).
- Small changes needed to kernel library to expose predictable post-layer checkpoints. Most transformer kernels already have natural layer boundaries; focus on making workspace allocations deterministic across variants.

Open questions / risks:
- Resource fragmentation: repeated preemption may reduce prefill batching efficiency and increase cost. Need careful SLO-driven throttles.
- Correctness edge cases: models with non-uniform layer semantics (custom layers) may not have safe preemption points; classifier heads or adapter modules complicate commit semantics.
- Implementation complexity: sequencer+kv-coordinator tight coupling increases code surface area in the hot path and risks regressions.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Spike: implement a minimal sequencer that can: accept requests, tag priority, and produce an interleaving plan; run synthetic workload to measure p95 improvement. Owner: Ethan Morales.
- KV-Coordinator prototype: implement read-fence API and per-layer commit markers. Owner: Chen Li.
- Kernel split API PR: propose small API in runtime kernel lib for preemption points. Owner: Maya Gupta.
- Experiment design doc for canary, including acceptance criteria and rollback triggers. Owner: Priya Nair.

Appendix: quick pseudocode for admission evaluation:

function should_interleave(prefill_batch, incoming_decode, gpu_state):
  remaining = prefill_batch.estimated_remaining_ms(gpu_state)
  decode_est = incoming_decode.estimated_step_ms
  if incoming_decode.priority == P0 and remaining > threshold_preempt_ms and prefill_batch.preemption_budget > 0:
    if kernel_compat(prefill_batch.next_kernel, decode_est.kernel_type):
      return true
  return false

Notes on experiments: keep preemption_budget conservative (default 2 preemptions per micro-batch) and slowly increase if interactive p99 remains above objective.
